about.title: San Joaquin Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Joaquin is a small farming community in western Fresno County, home to roughly 4,022 people, and a loss here is felt block by block. In 2024, the town's final crash records show zero traffic deaths, zero injury collisions and zero people injured. That is good news, and it also means that when a fatal loss does happen — on South Main Street, along Colorado Avenue or Idaho Avenue, in a field, at a job site or in a clinic — the family facing it may feel very much alone. California law gives a spouse, domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in after them. The clock generally runs two years from the date of death, and it moves faster when a public agency is involved. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the income your loved one would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive connects you with an independent attorney at no cost, so those questions reach someone equipped to answer them.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in San Joaquin Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family stands before anyone spends time on the wrong path.

items.title: The deadline is real, and sometimes shorter
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but if a city, county or state agency played a role, the window narrows considerably. Getting connected early protects that timeline.

items.title: A civil claim, separate from any criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not prosecutors file charges, your family's civil claim stands on its own and can seek funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: San Joaquin recorded no traffic deaths in 2024 — does that make a wrongful death claim harder to bring?
items.answer: No. Public crash counts describe what happened across the town in a given year; they have no bearing on the facts of your family's loss. A claim depends on what caused the death and who was responsible, whether that happened on South Main Street, on a farm outside town, or in a medical setting. An attorney evaluates your specific situation, not a citywide tally.

items.question: My father died and my mother is still living. Can I file the claim, or does she have to?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children share the first right to bring a wrongful death action, and they are generally expected to bring it together in a single case. If there is no spouse, partner or children, certain dependents and heirs may have standing instead. An attorney can explain how your family's specific situation fits these rules.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges in Fresno County. Should we wait until that case is finished?
items.answer: You do not have to wait, and waiting can be risky because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action with a different purpose: compensating your family for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. Connecting with an attorney early lets them preserve evidence and protect the timeline while the criminal matter proceeds on its own track.
